[1/4] Add career milestones evaluated at settlement and shown in the dossier and run legacy

impact_assessment.why: The career dossier records totals and recent runs, but there are no long-term goals; a player can finish many runs without a visible mastery ladder.
impact_assessment.benefits: Permanent milestone badges give replay goals, make unusual outcomes legible, and turn the run archive into evidence of progress.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: career.json gains an additive achievements list and run summaries gain a field; dependency: none; concurrency: settlement remains one-shot; state: old careers must load unlocked-empty and unlocks must never duplicate.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Evaluate only inside settle_career after stats update, append unique IDs, sanitize old payloads, keep the catalog in one module, and cover unlock rules, deduplication, persistence, CLI and API display with tests.

[1/4] Add a deterministic Daily Run with per-day best results in the career dossier

impact_assessment.why: Runs are seed-driven but the game offers no shared daily challenge; players have no reason to return on a given day or compare a fixed seed.
impact_assessment.benefits: A date-derived seed creates a fresh challenge every day, daily bests add a personal leaderboard, and the run archive gains a meaningful tag.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: engine/save state gains daily_key and career.json gains daily_best; dependency: none; concurrency: date is resolved once at run start; state: old saves and careers must default cleanly and a daily run must survive save/load.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Resolve the date at reset/start only, persist the key with the save, sanitize and cap daily bests on read, and cover determinism, persistence, settlement, CLI and API paths with tests.

[1/3] Replay archived run seeds from the terminal and Web career dossier

impact_assessment.why: The run archive stores seeds but offers no way to reuse them; players must copy a seed and start over manually.
impact_assessment.benefits: One explicit action revisits an interesting or daily seed, making the archive useful for practice and comparison.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new replay command/button only, no schema change; dependency: none; concurrency: replay replaces the live engine; state: a past daily key must not silently rewrite historical daily bests.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Replay as a normal run with the archived seed, ignore the archived daily key, require an explicit index or confirmation, and cover valid/invalid replay paths plus the existing reset API.

[1/3] Harden backup integrity and non-finite save/career metadata

impact_assessment.why: The crash-safe save claim depends on the shadow backup, but a corrupt primary can be copied over a good .bak before replacement; NaN/Infinity metadata can also crash archive rendering or career load.
impact_assessment.benefits: Recovery survives a corrupt primary, archives remain listable with damaged metadata, and malformed career numbers cannot take the dossier down.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: storage internals only, no save schema change; dependency: none; concurrency: single-user atomic writes; state: valid saves must behave exactly as before and career sanitization must keep good values.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate the primary before refreshing the backup, fall back to file mtime for unusable timestamps, reject non-finite daily values, and cover both corruption paths with failing-first tests.
